title: Power in a 46 Ω heater on 230 V rms
caption: I_rms = 230/46 = 5 A, the peak current is 5 × √2 = 7.1 A, and the average power is V_rmsI_rms = 1150 W. The instantaneous power p = v²/R swings between 0 and 2300.0000000000005 W, twice per cycle, and its average is exactly half the peak, 1150.0000000000002 W: that is why rms values work for power.
alt: Graph of instantaneous power against time: a curve that is never negative, between 0 and 2300.0000000000005 watts, repeating every 10 ms, with its average at 1150 W.
description: The horizontal axis is time in milliseconds; the vertical axis is the power in watts.
p = v²/R = 325² sin²(ωt)/46 = 2300.0000000000005 sin²(ωt) W: never negative, peaking at 2300.0000000000005 W.
Its average over a cycle is half the peak: 1150 W = V_rms × I_rms = 230 V × 5 A.
